elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) as redlined still obliges the Company (Customer) to pay HDI a "Termination Payment" on any Company termination, and 4.2(c) retains the eight-instalment payment mechanic; a Customer-payable liquidated amount therefore survives.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Redlined 4.2(a): the Termination Payment "shall be the Company's sole early termination fee and the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company under this Agreement"; the only Customer-payable stipulated sum in Section 4 is thus characterised as an early-termination fee triggered by Company termination.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Redlined 4.2(a) replaces the Net Sales formula with "shall not exceed the fees payable by the Company pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date" — an express three-months-of-fees ceiling on the Customer-payable amount.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Redlined 4.2(a) states the amount is "the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company under this Agreement"; the retained 4.2(b)-(c) only address a zero result and instalments and add no separate liquidated sum.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete on its face: 4.2(a) now contains a single Customer-payable early-termination fee, capped at three months of Section 3.1 fees, expressly stated to be the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company. Preferred level is not reached because a Customer-payable termination sum (with a retained quarterly instalment mechanic) survives.

Minimality is satisfied: the edit touches only the amount language in 4.2(a) and adds the sole-fee/sole-liquidated-amount wording required by fallback elements 1 and 3; 4.2(b) and 4.2(c) are retained verbatim and no survival tails, expense language, procedures, or other extras are introduced.

Intent is not preserved: the edit deletes the only computation mechanic in Section 4.2 and substitutes a ceiling only ("shall not exceed"), so the Termination Payment now has no determinable amount, and retained 4.2(b) — "Payment is determined pursuant to this Section 4.2 to be less than or equal to zero" — is left dangling because no determination under Section 4.2 remains capable of producing a zero or negative result. Repair in operative language: either state the payable amount (e.g., "an amount equal to [formula], provided that such amount shall not exceed the fees payable pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date") or conform/strike 4.2(b) so the zero-value machinery is not orphaned.

Ancillary drafting point for the drafter, not a separate element failure: 4.2(c) spreads the capped fee over eight quarterly instalments beginning 30 days after termination, which is retained original allocation and remains workable once the amount is made determinable.
